transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-28
Start: 16:00 EST
Duration: 48 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Oliver (Tidewater Head of IT), Rina (Sec Arch), Marcus (Platform)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Okay everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Oliver Grant: Oliver here.
[00:10] Rina Shah: Rina on my end.
[00:12] Marcus Lee: Marcus present.
[00:15] Maya Patel: Great. Jonas from our infra team is with me, he'll lead the SCIM mapping and role templates section.
[00:21] Jonas Reed: Hey all. Quick note, we'll try to keep this technical but tl;dr friendly.

Summary/goal: customer wants to validate SSO/SAML setup, SCIM provisioning readiness, and RBAC least-privilege mapping before staging pilot. Also confirm SOC2 artifact access, KMS/encryption model, and audit log retention for compliance.

[02:03] Maya: Rina, can you remind us of your top blockers? I know you mentioned data residency and audit retention in the intro email.
[02:11] Rina: Yeah, main things: 1) We need SOC2 Type II report and ISO27001 scope, 2) audit logs for all token/API operations retained 12 months, 3) SSO must be SAML with SCIM for provisioning and group sync, and 4) KMS integration—customer-managed keys if possible. Also, least-privilege for platform engineers vs auditors.
[02:32] Jonas: Got it. On the SOC2 and ISO docs we can share our compliance pack — will send a redacted SOC2 and the ISO attestation. For KMS we support customer KMS via cloud KMS or HSM for Private deployments; hosted can integrate with your KMS through a delegated key flow.
[02:48] Oliver: Delegated key flow — can you clarify? We don't want keys leaving our control.
[02:53] Jonas: Sure, for hosted we do envelope encryption: you keep the customer master key in your KMS, we get wrapped keys that we can't decrypt without the CMK. For Private deployments you can host everything in your VPC and bring-your-own-key with HSM. There's some nuance on key rotation and operator access.

[04:10] Marcus: For the SAML piece, is there a strict requirement on NameID format? Our IdP traditionally sends email as NameID, but some apps want persistent ID.
[04:20] Maya: We accept emailNameID or persistent; we can map attributes. Jonas, any gotchas?
[04:25] Jonas: Only that if you use transient NameID some SCIM provisioning flows won't map stable externalId — so for provisioning stable userId is recommended.

[05:00] Rina: On SCIM — we want group-based entitlements. We'll have groups in Okta and want group membership to map to roles: e.g., "ops-engineers" => developer role, "platform-admins" => admin, "audit" => read-only-audit. How are role templates handled?
[05:18] Jonas: We have role templates that are configurable per tenant. They show up as role IDs in the SCIM groups->roles mapping. We'll share a sample mapping file (CSV + JSON example). Ex: groupName maps to roleId:platform_developer. Important to also map service accounts separately as they need token scoping.
[05:45] Speaker 2: Uh-huh, and what about provisioning cadence?
[05:47] Maya: yeah, we usually recommend near real-time SCIM sync for user changes and periodic group sync every 5-15 minutes depending on your session TTLs.

[06:30] Marcus: Session TTLs — what's default for token expiration? We have strict session policies.
[06:35] Jonas: Default is 1 hour for short-lived tokens, refreshable via our API; for longer lived service tokens you can use scoped API keys with explicit expiry. We can set token lifetime to meet your policy.

[07:10] Rina: Audit logs—what is in the logs? We need admin actions, model inference requests (token-level?), policy changes, role changes, SCIM actions, SAML login attempts. Retention and exportability are key.
[07:24] Maya: We capture admin events, provisioning events, role changes, config changes, and a per-route latency/cost breakdown. We do not log raw customer prompt content unless requested and explicitly enabled for debugging—default is only metadata.
[07:40] Rina: Hmm, we need to be careful about PII in logs. If inference metadata includes user IDs, that's okay; prompt content retention is a no-go unless it is explicitly part of an agreed SOC procedure.
[07:53] Jonas: Understood. We'll provide a log schema doc and options: masked prompts, metadata-only, or full with retention controls. For SOC2 evidence, we can show the logging pipeline and redaction controls.

[09:10] Oliver: On SAML cert rotation — what's the cadence and how do we avoid downtime?
[09:16] Jonas: We support metadata exchange and rolling cert updates. You can provide an alternate signing cert in the metadata so we can rotate without breaking logins. We'll share a playbook.

[10:02] Maya: Let's dig into role least-privilege mapping. How many distinct roles do you want initially?
[10:09] Marcus: Probably three: admin, dev/platform, and audit. Maybe a service account role for CI.
[10:15] Rina: Also need a support role that has limited troubleshooting access but can't retrieve PII or change billing.
[10:21] Jonas: That's reasonable. Best practice: small number of high-trust admin principals, broad use of scoped service tokens, and use of temporary elevation—JIT—for dangerous ops. Our platform supports RBAC with fine-grained permissions per API route and resource-level scoping.

[11:15] Speaker 3: Are we able to restrict redwood console access by IP/VPN?
[11:19] Maya: For Dedicated and Private yes, you can restrict console access via IP allowlists and VPC peering. Hosted customers can have IP restrictions for admin endpoints and SSO enforced.

[12:05] Rina: Data residency: we have data centers in EU only for production; does Redwood host EU regions with VPC isolation?
[12:12] Jonas: Yes, we run regional deployments — EU, NA, APAC. For production with residency requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private in your region. Hosted EU ensures data is persisted in EU region and we can confirm backups and logs residency.

[13:02] Oliver: We also need to know the encryption in transit and at rest specifics. TLS v1.2+? Managed disk encryption?
[13:10] Jonas: TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers, mTLS available for service-to-service in Private. At rest disks are encrypted with customer KMS if BYOK, otherwise provider-managed keys with CMKs. We'll include the encryption matrix in the docs.

[14:25] Marcus: For SCIM attributes: required attributes? We use firstName,lastName,email,employeeNumber; externalId; groups.
[14:34] Maya: For our SCIM, required: userName (email preferred), externalId if you want stable mapping, displayName optional. We'll take employeeNumber as an additional attribute to map.

[15:05] Rina: Group sync — do you support nested groups? Our Okta uses nested groups heavily.
[15:12] Jonas: We support flat groups natively. For nested groups we can either flatten during provisioning or map nested groups to composite role rules. We'll show a mapping example.

[16:00] Maya: Any blockers on your side to start staging?
[16:04] Marcus: Main blocker is getting the SCIM mapping and a staging tenant. Also need the SAML cert.
[16:09] Maya: We'll get that to you. Jonas will send the mapping and template.

[17:45] Jonas: Quick demo note — when mapping groups to roles, we include an allowlist flag and a default-role for orphaned users. Highly recommend a default read-only role for safety.

[18:20] Rina: About audit retention again — is 12 months standard? Does it cost extra?
[18:26] Maya: 12 months is common for enterprise customers. There's an add-on for extended retention beyond our base 3-6 months depending on plan. We'll include pricing options.

[19:10] Oliver: Any SOC2 exceptions or controls we should be aware of?
[19:15] Jonas: Nothing major; we have control descriptions for access control, change management, incident mgmt. We'll send the SOC2 attestations and a controls mapping spreadsheet to show how our controls map to your requirements.

[20:40] Speaker 1: Regarding SAML attributes, can we pass group membership in the assertion instead of SCIM?
[20:48] Jonas: You can — but group-in-assertion is brittle for large orgs. SCIM gives canonical state and is preferred. If you prefer assertion groups for a quick pilot we support it, but SCIM is the recommended long-term solution.

[22:10] Marcus: Do roles created via SCIM have UUIDs or name-based keys? Our automation expects stable IDs.
[22:16] Jonas: They have stable role IDs (UUIDs) which are returned by the API and should be referenced by automation. We'll provide example APIs and a mapping export.

[23:50] Rina: On just-in-time elevation — can you require approval workflow?
[23:55] Maya: We integrate with your ticketing/approval flows for elevation or you can plug our built-in approval step. It's optional.

[25:00] Oliver: For compliance evidence we need: SOC2, ISO cert, penetration test summary, and the audit log schema.
[25:07] Maya: We'll package that as a security pack and redact customer-sensitive items.

[26:50] Jonas: One thing to call out — prompt logging. By default we don't persist prompts; there's a debug logging mode for evals. For SOC2 you'd want to capture metadata and request IDs; if you require prompt retention we can enable with strict access controls and masking.

[28:20] Marcus: If we enable prompt retention for debugging, who can access them?
[28:24] Jonas: Only users with the audit role and a special data-access permission, logged and auditable; and we suggest time-limited access.

[30:02] Rina: Are there any rate-limits or burst capacity concerns for SCIM writes?
[30:07] Jonas: SCIM endpoints are rate-limited for protection; for initial syncs we can temporarily increase quotas or provide a bulk user import API to avoid throttling.

[31:40] Maya: Let's recap next steps quick. Jonas will send SAML metadata and role templates; I'll send SCIM mapping and sample CSV; Rina will confirm retention policy and data residency constraints; Marcus will create staging tenant and add test users.

[32:02] Speaker 2: And timeline?
[32:05] Oliver: We aim to have staging up and tests complete in 2 weeks.

[32:12] Maya: Sounds good. We'll target the dates in the action items. Anything else?

[33:00] Rina: One last question — on support access for troubleshooting, can Redwood request temporary access to our staging environment?
[33:07] Jonas: We can do temporary support sessions with explicit audit entries and time-limited tokens. Preferably via a support playbook we both sign off.

[34:30] Marcus: Ok, please include the playbook sample.

[35:20] Maya: We'll bundle the security pack, playbook, SCIM/SCHEMA docs, SAML metadata, and role templates in one email.

[36:00] Oliver: Great. Appreciate the detail.
[36:05] Rina: Thanks all.

[36:30] Maya: Thanks everybody, I'll send meeting notes and the next steps.

Closing:
Recap delivered, action items assigned (see action_items), agreed timeline ~2 weeks to staging verification, follow-up security pack and SAML/SCIM artifacts to be delivered by Redwood.

End of recording.
